stem.en: The Cell Theory is credited to several scientists over many years, not to one discoverer. What does this tell you about how it was built?

text.en: The earlier scientists were wrong and the last one corrected them.

feedback.en: Each one added a real part. Later work extended the earlier work.

text.en: Each one added a part, and the parts made one theory.

feedback.en: Yes. Schleiden added plants, Schwann added animals, and Virchow added where new cells come from.

text.en: Nobody was sure enough to claim the whole idea for themselves alone.

feedback.en: Shared credit shows how the evidence grew. It does not show doubt.

text.en: It is still only a guess, and it has never been tested by anyone.

feedback.en: A scientific theory is a well-tested explanation, not a guess.

explanation.en: Schleiden reported that all plants are made of cells, Schwann that all animals are, and Virchow that new cells come only from pre-existing cells. Their work together led to the Cell Theory.

hints.en: What did Schleiden, Schwann and Virchow each add?
